name: Industrial high-pressure ammonia synthesis
summary: In 1913 BASF opened at Oppau the first industrial plant making ammonia directly from nitrogen and hydrogen under high pressure, the basis of today's synthetic fertilizer.
description: Industrial direct catalytic synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at high pressure using catalysts and pressure-resistant industrial equipment.
tier_reason: Large-scale fixed-nitrogen production supports successive agricultural and chemical-production systems, not merely one factory.

impact.note: Synthetic nitrogen came to feed about half of humanity and founded high-pressure industrial chemistry, one line rather than many fields; generativity 2 implies tier 1, not the reviewed tier 0.

why: Fertilizer and explosives depended on limited Chilean nitrate, and once Haber showed the high-pressure reaction worked, BASF saw a market in fixing atmospheric nitrogen.

market.note: BASF describes operating an industrial ammonia plant that supplied feedstock for industrial fertilizer production; this establishes commercial applicability, not the first external sale.

evidence.supports: Describes operation of the plant and ammonia as feedstock for industrial fertilizer production.

date.basis: BASF dates the Oppau ammonia-synthesis plant’s start of operation to 1913.

events.statement: BASF’s Oppau works put an industrial ammonia-synthesis plant into operation.
events.scope: BASF’s industrial high-pressure synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at the Oppau plant.
events.population: BASF operators producing ammonia at the Oppau works
events.caveats: Manufacturer historical summary; exact start date, downstream batches and first sale are not established. It does not show all fertilizer production moved to this process.

evidence.supports: Dates BASF’s Oppau industrial ammonia synthesis operation to 1913.

date.label: 9 February 1928
date.basis: NIA reports that the Notodden ammonia-synthesis plant began operation on 9 February 1928.

events.statement: Norsk Hydro put its Notodden ammonia-synthesis plant into operation.
applications: industrial ammonia synthesis for calcium-nitrate production
events.population: Norsk Hydro Notodden ammonia plant operators
events.caveats: The local plant used NEC and international components; this event does not establish that Oppau equipment was physically transferred to Notodden.

evidence.supports: States that the company changed its calcium-nitrate production route from arc fixation to ammonia; dates Notodden synthesis start to 9 February 1928 and the last local arc furnace to 1934.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. community_entry.community: BASF operators producing ammonia at the Oppau works
community_entry.rationale: The 1913 Oppau operation demonstrates industrial implementation beyond earlier high-pressure laboratory trials; the event is scoped to that plant.
community_entry.caveats: Manufacturer historical summary; exact start date, downstream batches and first sale are not established. It does not show all fertilizer production moved to this process.

caveats: The 1913 Oppau plant was a documented industrial deployment of a process developed from earlier laboratory work; preceding electric-arc and cyanamide routes also fixed nitrogen. Exact earliest commercial availability is unresolved.

links.statement: At Notodden, Norsk Hydro shifted calcium-nitrate manufacture toward ammonia synthesis; the new synthesis plant operated from 1928 while the last local Birkeland–Eyde furnace continued until 1934.
links.scope: Norsk Hydro’s Notodden transition from the 1920s to 1934.
links.alternatives: Electric-arc fixation continued locally during the transition; calcium cyanamide and natural nitrate were other available routes.
links.caveats: The Notodden plant used NEC-associated technology; the relationship is to the generic direct-ammonia process, not a claim that the 1913 Oppau plant or its equipment was relocated.
links.timing: The 1907 arc deployment preceded the 1928 Notodden ammonia operation; both operated during the transition.
